legal.accessibilityCommitmentBody: AU-IBAR is committed to ensuring that the Animal Resources Information System (ARIS) is accessible to all users across the 55 African Union Member States, regardless of ability, technology, or connectivity conditions. As a continental platform serving diverse populations, accessibility is a core design principle, not an afterthought.
legal.accessibilityStandardsBody: ARIS strives to conform to the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 at the AA level. We continuously work to improve the platform's accessibility in alignment with the AU Digital Transformation Strategy's principle of inclusive digital services.
legal.accessibilityMultilingualBody: ARIS is available in four official languages of the African Union: English, French (Français), Portuguese (Português), and Arabic (العربية) — with full Right-to-Left (RTL) layout support. Users can switch languages at any time. The mobile application also supports all four languages.
legal.accessibilityVisual1: High Contrast Mode — The platform automatically detects system-level accessibility settings and can enable high contrast color schemes for improved readability
legal.accessibilityVisual2: Color Independence — Information is never conveyed by color alone; icons, labels, and patterns complement color-coded elements
legal.accessibilityVisual3: Scalable Typography — Text sizes use relative units (rem/sp) and respect browser and device font size preferences
legal.accessibilityVisual4: Domain Color Coding — Each of the 9 business domains uses a distinct color with sufficient contrast ratios, always paired with text labels and icons
legal.accessibilityNav1: Keyboard Navigation — All interactive elements are accessible via keyboard. Focus indicators are visible when navigating with Tab/Shift+Tab
legal.accessibilityNav2: Screen Reader Support — Semantic HTML structure with proper heading hierarchy, ARIA labels, and landmark regions for screen reader compatibility
legal.accessibilityNav3: Clear Form Labels — All form inputs include visible labels, placeholder text, and error messages that are programmatically associated with their fields
legal.accessibilityNav4: Skip Navigation — Skip-to-content links allow keyboard users to bypass repetitive navigation elements
legal.accessibilityMobile1: TalkBack Support — The Android application is built with Jetpack Compose, which provides native accessibility support for Android's TalkBack screen reader
legal.accessibilityMobile2: Biometric Authentication — Alternative authentication methods (fingerprint, PIN) accommodate users who may have difficulty typing complex passwords
legal.accessibilityMobile3: Offline Operation — The app works without internet connectivity, essential for field agents in remote areas with limited infrastructure
legal.accessibilityMobile4: Adaptive Layout — The app adapts to different screen sizes (phones and tablets) with responsive grid layouts
legal.accessibilityMobile5: Touch Target Size — Interactive elements meet minimum touch target sizes (48dp) for comfortable interaction
legal.accessibilityConnectivityBody: Recognizing that many users operate in areas with limited or intermittent internet connectivity, ARIS includes:
legal.accessibilityConnectivity1: Offline-First Architecture — The mobile app stores data locally and synchronizes when connectivity is available
legal.accessibilityConnectivity2: Offline Maps — Map tiles can be downloaded in advance for use without internet access, with 11 predefined regional presets covering all African regions
legal.accessibilityConnectivity3: Low Bandwidth Optimization — Images are compressed, data payloads are minimized, and incremental sync reduces data usage
legal.accessibilityConnectivity4: Connectivity Indicator — A clear visual banner informs users when they are working offline, so they understand their data will sync later
legal.accessibilityData1: Export Formats — Data can be exported in CSV and JSON formats compatible with assistive technologies and standard data analysis tools
legal.accessibilityData2: Structured Tables — Data tables include proper headers, sorting controls, and pagination for manageable data consumption
legal.accessibilityData3: Chart Alternatives — Dashboard charts and visualizations include text-based KPI summaries that convey the same information in non-visual formats
legal.accessibilityLimitationsBody: We are aware of the following accessibility limitations that we are actively working to address:
legal.accessibilityLimitation1: Some complex data visualization charts (Canvas-rendered) may not be fully accessible to screen readers; text-based alternatives are provided where possible
legal.accessibilityLimitation2: The embedded Leaflet map on the continental dashboard requires mouse or touch interaction; a data table alternative is planned
legal.accessibilityLimitation3: PDF export formatting may not be fully optimized for screen reader consumption
legal.accessibilityTesting3: Screen reader testing (TalkBack on Android, NVDA/JAWS on desktop)
legal.accessibilityTesting5: Testing across multiple device types and screen sizes
legal.accessibilityFeedbackBody: We welcome feedback on the accessibility of ARIS. If you encounter accessibility barriers or have suggestions for improvement, please contact us:
legal.accessibilityFeedbackAddress: Kenindia Business Park, Museum Hill, P.O. Box 30786-00100, Nairobi, Kenya
legal.accessibilityFeedbackResponse: We aim to respond to accessibility feedback within 5 business days and to resolve identified barriers in a timely manner.
legal.accessibilityImprovementBody: AU-IBAR is committed to continuously improving the accessibility of ARIS as part of our mandate to serve all 55 Member States equitably. Accessibility reviews are conducted with each major platform update, and user feedback directly informs our improvement priorities.
legal.privacy1Body: The African Union Interafrican Bureau for Animal Resources (AU-IBAR), headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, operates the Animal Resources Information System (ARIS) — a continental digital platform serving 55 Member States and 8 Regional Economic Communities (RECs). This Privacy Policy describes how we collect, use, protect, and share information through the ARIS platform, including the web application (au-aris.org) and the ARIS mobile application.
legal.privacy2Address: Kenindia Business Park, Museum Hill, P.O. Box 30786-00100, Nairobi, Kenya
legal.privacy31Intro: When your organization registers you as an ARIS user, we collect:
legal.privacy31Item1: Full name, email address, and professional role
legal.privacy31Item2: Organizational affiliation (Member State, REC, or AU-IBAR)
legal.privacy31Item3: User role and domain access permissions
legal.privacy31Item4: Language preference (English, French, Portuguese, or Arabic)
legal.privacy32Body: ARIS collects official animal resources data submitted by authorized national officers across 9 business domains: Animal Health, Livestock Production, Fisheries & Aquaculture, Trade & SPS, Wildlife & Biodiversity, Apiculture, Climate & Environment, Governance, and Knowledge Management. This data is submitted under the authority of each Member State and remains under national sovereignty.
legal.privacy33Intro: The ARIS mobile application may collect GPS coordinates when:
legal.privacy33Item1: Recording field observations (outbreak locations, farm coordinates)
legal.privacy33Item2: Tracking transhumance corridors and field agent movements
legal.privacy33Item3: Geotagging photographs taken during field operations
legal.privacy33Body: Location collection requires explicit user permission and can be disabled at any time through device settings. Location data is only collected while actively performing field operations.
legal.privacy34Item3: Network connectivity status (for offline sync management)
legal.privacy34Item4: Crash logs and error reports (for application improvement)
legal.privacy35Body: Field agents may capture photographs as evidence for surveillance events, outbreak reports, or field inspections. These photos are stored securely and associated with the relevant data submission. EXIF metadata (including GPS coordinates and timestamp) may be retained for verification purposes.
legal.privacy4Intro: We use the collected information to:
legal.privacy4Item1: Operate and improve the ARIS platform and its services
legal.privacy4Item2: Enable data collection, validation, and reporting across Member States
legal.privacy4Item3: Generate continental dashboards, analytics, and KPI reports
legal.privacy4Item5: Support interoperability with international systems (WAHIS, EMPRES, FAOSTAT)
legal.privacy4Item6: Send push notifications for outbreak alerts and campaign updates
legal.privacy4Item7: Provide technical support and resolve issues
legal.privacy4Item8: Ensure platform security and prevent unauthorized access
legal.privacy5Intro: All data in ARIS is classified according to four levels, in line with the AU Digital Transformation Strategy:
legal.privacy5Partner: Shared with authorized organizations (WOAH, FAO, WHO)
legal.privacy5Body: Data classified as RESTRICTED or CONFIDENTIAL is never shared publicly. Official disease notifications to WOAH via WAHIS are made exclusively by authorized WAHIS Focal Points, respecting national sovereignty.
legal.privacy6Body: ARIS operates under the principle of federated subsidiarity: data is produced and validated at the country level. Each Member State retains sovereignty over its national data. AU-IBAR consolidates data at the continental level only after it has been officially validated through the 4-level workflow. No country-level data is published without the explicit approval of the national authority (Chief Veterinary Officer or designated official).
legal.privacy7Intro: We implement industry-standard security measures including:
legal.privacy7Item1: End-to-end encryption (TLS 1.3) for all data in transit
legal.privacy7Item2: AES-256 encryption for sensitive data at rest
legal.privacy7Item3: JWT RS256 token-based authentication with automatic expiration
legal.privacy7Item4: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA TOTP) for privileged accounts
legal.privacy7Item5: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with 8 distinct roles
legal.privacy7Item6: Comprehensive audit trail for all data mutations
legal.privacy7Item7: Encrypted local storage on mobile devices (EncryptedSharedPreferences)
legal.privacy7Item8: Biometric authentication option on mobile devices
legal.privacy7Item9: Regular security assessments and penetration testing
legal.privacy8Body: Animal resources data is retained for the duration necessary to fulfill ARIS's mandate as the AU continental information system. Historical data is essential for trend analysis, epidemiological modelling, and policy evaluation. User accounts are maintained for the duration of employment in an authorized role and may be deactivated upon request from the relevant national authority.
legal.privacy9Intro: Authorized users have the right to:
legal.privacy9Item2: Request correction of inaccurate personal data
legal.privacy9Item3: Request account deactivation through their national administrator
legal.privacy9Item4: Export their submitted data in standard formats (CSV, JSON)
legal.privacy9Item5: Opt out of non-essential push notifications
legal.privacy10Body: ARIS servers are hosted in secure data centers. Data may be transferred between Member States and AU-IBAR headquarters in accordance with the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention, 2014) and applicable national data protection laws.
legal.privacy11Body: The ARIS web platform uses essential cookies for session management and authentication. We do not use third-party advertising cookies. Anonymous usage analytics may be collected to improve the platform experience.
legal.privacy12Body: ARIS is a professional platform designed for authorized government officials and organizational personnel. It is not intended for use by individuals under 18 years of age.
legal.privacy13Body: We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes in our practices or applicable regulations. Users will be notified of significant changes through the ARIS platform. The "Last updated" date at the top indicates the most recent revision.
legal.privacy14Intro: For questions about this Privacy Policy or data protection matters, contact:
legal.privacy14Address: Kenindia Business Park, Museum Hill, P.O. Box 30786-00100, Nairobi, Kenya
legal.terms1Body: By accessing or using the Animal Resources Information System (ARIS), operated by the African Union Interafrican Bureau for Animal Resources (AU-IBAR), you agree to be bound by these Terms of Service. ARIS is a restricted-access platform; access is granted only to authorized personnel of AU Member States, Regional Economic Communities (RECs), and partner organizations.
legal.terms2Intro: ARIS is a continental digital infrastructure providing:
legal.terms2Item1: Data collection and reporting for animal resources across 9 business domains
legal.terms2Item2: A 4-level data validation workflow (National Data Steward → CVO → REC → AU-IBAR)
legal.terms2Item3: Continental dashboards, analytics, and KPI monitoring
legal.terms2Item4: Interoperability with international systems (WAHIS, EMPRES, FAOSTAT, FishStatJ, CITES)
legal.terms2Item5: Mobile field data collection with offline capability
legal.terms2Item7: Real-time outbreak alerts and push notifications
legal.terms31Body: ARIS accounts are created by authorized administrators (National Admins, REC Admins, or AU-IBAR Super Admins). Self-registration is not available. Each user is assigned a specific role determining their access level and permissions.
legal.terms32Analyst: Read-only access for research and analysis
legal.terms32FieldAgent: Mobile data collection in the field
legal.terms33Item1: Maintaining the confidentiality of their login credentials
legal.terms33Item2: Enabling Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) when required by their administrator
legal.terms33Item3: Reporting any suspected unauthorized access immediately
legal.terms33Item4: Logging out of shared or public devices after each session
legal.terms33Item5: Using the PIN lock or biometric authentication feature on mobile devices
legal.terms41Intro: Users authorized to submit data acknowledge that their submissions represent official information from their respective organizations. All data must pass ARIS quality gates before publication:
legal.terms41Item1: Completeness — Key fields must be filled
legal.terms41Item2: Temporal consistency — Dates must be logically ordered
legal.terms41Item3: Geographic consistency — Locations must be valid
legal.terms41Item4: Codes & vocabularies — Must use approved referentials
legal.terms41Item7: Auditability — Source and validation status documented
legal.terms42Body: Official disease notifications to the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) via the WAHIS system are exclusively the responsibility of designated WAHIS Focal Points. ARIS facilitates the preparation of WAHIS-ready data packages but does not automatically submit notifications to WOAH. Each notification remains a sovereign act of the Member State.
legal.terms5Item1: Share login credentials with unauthorized individuals
legal.terms5Item2: Submit knowingly false or misleading data
legal.terms5Item3: Attempt to access data outside their authorized scope
legal.terms5Item4: Use automated tools to scrape or extract bulk data without authorization
legal.terms5Item5: Circumvent security controls, access restrictions, or audit mechanisms
legal.terms5Item6: Use ARIS data for commercial purposes without written authorization from AU-IBAR
legal.terms5Item7: Publish RESTRICTED or CONFIDENTIAL data without proper authorization
legal.terms5Item8: Interfere with the platform's operation or other users' access
legal.terms6Body: The ARIS platform, including its software, design, documentation, and analytical methodologies, is the property of AU-IBAR. The data submitted by Member States remains under the sovereignty of the submitting country. Aggregated and analytical outputs produced by ARIS are co-owned by AU-IBAR and the contributing Member States, subject to the data classification rules.
legal.terms7Intro: All actions within ARIS are logged in a comprehensive audit trail, including:
legal.terms7Item2: Validation approvals and rejections with reasons
legal.terms7Body: The audit trail is immutable and may be reviewed for compliance, dispute resolution, or security investigations.
legal.terms8Body: AU-IBAR endeavors to maintain ARIS availability 24/7. However, we reserve the right to perform scheduled maintenance (typically communicated in advance) and cannot guarantee uninterrupted service. The mobile application includes offline capabilities to ensure data collection can continue during connectivity disruptions.
legal.terms9Intro: AU-IBAR or the relevant national administrator may suspend or terminate a user account for:
legal.terms9Item1: Violation of these Terms of Service
legal.terms9Item3: Security breaches or unauthorized access attempts
legal.terms9Item4: End of official mandate or employment
legal.terms9Item5: Request from the user's supervising authority
legal.terms10Body: ARIS is provided "as is" for official use by AU Member States. AU-IBAR shall not be liable for decisions made based on data within the platform. Users and Member States are responsible for verifying the accuracy of data before using it for official notifications, policy decisions, or public communications. Analytical dashboards carry appropriate provenance disclaimers.
legal.terms11Intro: These Terms are governed by the applicable frameworks of the African Union, including:
legal.terms11Item3: AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection (Malabo Convention)
legal.terms11Item6: Policy Framework for Pastoralism in Africa (PFRS)
legal.terms12Body: AU-IBAR reserves the right to update these Terms of Service. Users will be notified of material changes through the ARIS platform. Continued use of the platform after notification constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.
legal.terms13Intro: For questions about these Terms of Service, contact:
legal.terms13Address: Kenindia Business Park, Museum Hill, P.O. Box 30786-00100, Nairobi, Kenya
